Subject: Seasonal commitment phasing + reseller settlement timing

Hi Liz / Procurement team,

Great talking earlier — appreciate you outlining the winter surge and the pilot window in Q3. Based on our call I put together a short proposal for how Redwood can structure the private offer and the reseller settlement cadence so SkyHealth can scale predictably during seasonal spikes. High level:

- Commit phasing: split the annual commitment into three tranches — Q3 pilot (20%), Q4 seasonal uplift (40%), Q1 baseline (40%). This lets you ramp capacity and only increase committed spend if the pilot hits the targets.
- Settlement timing for reseller (you indicated using an existing reseller): we can support monthly invoicing with a 30-day settlement period; alternatively we can use quarterly reconciliation if your reseller needs fewer invoices.
- Channel margin: we propose an initial 10% reseller margin with a seasonal uplift credit (one-time bonus) tied to usage thresholds; we can increase to 12% on Q4 uplift if SkyHealth hits the agreed surge volume.

Attachments: proposal PDF and commit schedule.

Ask: can you confirm whether SkyHealth requires reseller invoices to flow through your procurement system (PO number on each invoice) or whether quarterly summary invoices + one PO per quarter are acceptable? Also tagging your reseller contact here will help me confirm flow and seller fees.

Happy to jump back on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Thanks Sean — this looks like a useful starting point. A few clarifying questions from procurement and billing: 

1) Invoice cadence: our AP team prefers monthly invoices for visibility, but our reseller contract historically requires net-45 settlement for pass-through invoices. Can Redwood do monthly invoice generation with a net-30 payment term while the reseller settles on net-45?

2) Reseller onboarding: please include Tom from AWS partners on follow-up so we can confirm if marketplace routing forces any specific invoice/PO fields.

3) Margin qualification: is the seasonal uplift credit applied as a one-time rebate or a change to the per-unit reseller margin for the uplift period? Our finance team needs that to model net cost.

If you can summarize two concrete settlement options (monthly net-30 with reseller net-45 or quarterly reconciliation) and how margins/credits appear on invoices, we can fast-track vendor paperwork.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Seasonal commitment phasing + reseller settlement timing — ops + billing options

Sean / Ben / Naomi / Liz — wrote up three practical options given current marketplace constraints and our channel economics. High level recommendations below; see attachment (commit_phasing_schedule.xlsx) for numbers.

Option A — Monthly billing to SkyHealth, Redwood pays reseller monthly (recommended)
- Redwood issues monthly invoice to SkyHealth (net-30). Invoice shows: list price by SKU, reseller margin as a separate negative line (10% of list), seasonal uplift credit as a separate credit line if triggered.
- Redwood pays reseller monthly net-30 based on billed usage. Reseller can set their own payment terms with SkyHealth but Redwood will not delay settlement in our reconciliation.
- Pros: predictable cashflow for SkyHealth and reseller; minimal bookkeeping for SkyHealth.
- Cons: reseller may need to accept earlier settlement compared to their legacy net-45; we can provide a one-time settlement fee to cover administrative friction.

Option B — Monthly invoice generation, Redwood holds funds for reseller until net-45
- Redwood invoices SkyHealth monthly (net-30) but retains reseller portion in a short-hold account and disburses to reseller on net-45 schedule to match their existing process. Seasonal credits are applied to SkyHealth invoice and reconciled when we disburse to reseller.
- Pros: aligns with reseller cashflow expectations.
- Cons: Redwood carries short-term settlement risk; requires compliance/finance approval for holding distribution funds. Possible extra accounting steps for marketplace-originated transactions (AWS/GCP may restrict intermediate holds).

Option C — Quarterly reconciliation / one PO per quarter
- SkyHealth receives monthly usage statements but is invoiced quarterly. Reseller receives quarterly settlement. Seasonal uplift applied as an adjustment in the quarter-end reconciliation.
- Pros: minimal operational churn for the reseller.
- Cons: slower cashflow, worse for SkyHealth visibility.

Channel margin & uplift mechanics: our standard flow is to present the reseller margin as a clearly labeled line item on the invoice; seasonal uplift can be issued as a one-time rebate (credit memo) or temporarily increase per-unit margin for the uplift period. Finance recommendation: use a credit memo (rebate) — it is easier for bookkeeping and makes the uplift auditable. If you need the margin increased in-contract for the uplift window, legal will need to reflect that in the private offer terms.

Marketplace notes: AWS marketplace private offers generally require the partner/reseller to accept settlement routing in advance; for GCP/Azure private offers the constraints are similar but can vary by partner. If settlement retention is required by the reseller (Option B), we need to confirm whether marketplace policy permits short-term disbursement holds — I recommend we confirm with Tom (cc'd) and Procurement.

Recommendation: Option A (monthly invoicing + monthly reseller payout) with a one-time settlement friction fee (small) unless the reseller confirms they cannot change their net terms. If the reseller cannot, Option B is possible but will require finance sign-off and an updated private offer flow.

Cc Naomi for tax/withholding considerations. Ben — can you confirm expected margin impact if we move the uplift from a credit memo to an in-contract margin raise?

—Camila

Liz / Tom / Procurement — thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary and next steps: 

1) Settlement path: per Camila's recommendation, default to Option A — monthly invoices to SkyHealth, Redwood pays reseller monthly (we will issue a small one-time settlement fee to the reseller to cover admin change). If Tom confirms his reseller cannot accept earlier settlement, we will fall back to Option B after finance approval.

2) Seasonal uplift: will be issued as a credit memo (one-time rebate) applied on the invoice following the month the threshold is met. If SkyHealth prefers an in-contract margin uplift instead, legal will need to update the private offer language and it will delay sign-off.

3) Doc flow: I attached the updated private offer terms (Redwood_terms_private_offer_v2.docx). If this looks good, please confirm and we will send via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABC-REDWOOD-SKYHEALTH

4) Action items for SkyHealth: please confirm preferred settlement option (Option A confirmed here unless you request otherwise), provide reseller billing contact and PO routing requirements, and confirm whether you need monthly line-item detail or a summarized invoice.

If we get confirmation today we can get legal & finance sign-off and have the DocuSign packet out tomorrow.

Thanks — appreciate the speed on this.
